Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high fidelity implementable UI design concept for Dreamy Debugger, an internal Unity mobile game debugger. This is a proposed design, NOT an actual running screenshot. Landscape 16:10 presentation image, very high resolution, precise readable English UI labels. Flat front-facing app screens, no perspective, no photographed hardware, no glossy device frames, no decorative illustration, no glow, no glass blur, no gradients. Quiet dark graphite surfaces (#16171A background, #202126 cards, #303238 borders), warm ivory (#F4EFEA) text, muted grey (#A5A3A2), strongly recognizable rich Dreamy red (#9E1008) header and coral red (#E95345) primary buttons and active indicators. Red stays the MAIN brand color. Charts have semantic mint/amber colors independent of the red brand. Clean Roboto-like sans serif, tabular numbers, consistent 8-unit spacing, modest 6-8px corner radius, thin crisp separators, sharp icons. Useful diagnostic density; approachable and professional. One Dreamy logo per app screen in the upper left using the supplied existing italic white wordmark identity; no author info or promotional banner. The reference banner is a LOGO REFERENCE ONLY, not a background to repeat. Baseline screenshots are PROBLEM/FEATURE REFERENCES ONLY; redesign their layout completely. Never add Report Bug, Gmail, Theme Setup, vendor branding, giant banner, pie charts, arbitrary admin dashboard KPIs, remote command execution or a subscription/profile avatar. Screens must look practical to build with Unity uGUI. No repeated action button for the same function. All mock values are synthetic. No long explanations in the image. Heading outside the screen: DREAMY DEBUGGER / DESIGN CONCEPT. Small footer outside screens: PROPOSED UI - NOT IMPLEMENTED.
Asset: board 01, runtime cheat workspace across landscape and portrait. Compose one large landscape app screen occupying the left 70 percent and one tall portrait app screen occupying right 28 percent, with legible labels and generous gap. Both show the SAME coherent theme and data. Label the views Landscape and Portrait outside screens.
Landscape app: compact dark-red top header with white Dreamy wordmark at left, a hamburger, small title Cheats, and pin and close buttons clearly separated on the right. Exactly four runtime navigation destinations: Cheats (active coral/red), Console with small count 3, Performance, System. Left sidebar 160px with icon plus label, active dark red row, no second logo in sidebar. Main content starts with title Cheat options, subtitle Game-owned controls, then search field Search options and compact chips All / Pinned / Economy / Gameplay. Content is a purposeful two-column layout, not a grid of unrelated dashboards.
Main card Economy, with small pin icon. In that card a resource sub-section Coins with label Balance and large clearly readable 9,825. Below, a tight coherent input group Grant amount [ minus ] [ 100 ] [ plus ] next to a red Add coins button. Same card second resource Gems, Balance 240, amount 10, red Add gems button. A muted inline success message Coins updated and a small last-updated time sit below, no toast covering content.
Second card Entitlements: row No Ads, readable Owned status pill, disabled Owned action (not a toggle which would falsely imply revoke). Third card Gameplay: God mode real switch Off, Time scale 1.00 with slider and reset icon, Difficulty Normal dropdown. Bottom compact collapsed foldout Debugger tools; do not put Build GUID above game cheats. Slim bottom status bar INTERNAL with small lock icon, Development, sandbox scene MainScene.
Portrait app 390 logical px wide: compact red header with hamburger / Dreamy logo / pin / close; title Cheats on own content line, Search options, All / Economy chips, Coins resource card with 9,825 and same amount 100 and Add coins. No Ads ownership row and Gameplay foldout beneath. No permanent sidebar on portrait. Touch controls visibly comfortable (48 logical units), not miniature desktop widgets. User can scroll; content never collides with close or pin. No bottom navigation competing with hamburger. No fake HUD behind panel; HUD hides when panel opens. Make the portrait layout spacious but not empty.

Asset: board 02, console triage and compact performance HUD. Compose LEFT 62 percent one large landscape Console app screen; RIGHT 35 percent three separate HUD size examples on a uniform muted slate game-placeholder rectangle. Label right column HUD / visible only when enabled, and example sizes FPS ONLY, COMPACT, DETAILED outside each HUD, not giant in the HUD. Keep exact same typography/palette as runtime cheat board.
Console app has a thin dark red header with one white Dreamy logo left, hamburger, title Console, pin and close right. Left navigation Cheats / Console(active) / Performance / System. Filter toolbar Search logs; severity chips All 42, Errors 3, Warnings 7, Info 32; small Collapse control and Clear icon. Main area is a scan-friendly chronological log list with timestamp column, severity icon and message column, repeat-count badge on the right, avoiding full red backgrounds on every error. Three visible rows: 12:04:32 Error Wallet balance unavailable with repeat badge 3; 12:04:31 Warning Slow frame 52 ms; 12:04:30 Info MainScene ready. Selected first row uses muted red tint with left red rule. A clearly separated lower detail pane shows Error, Wallet balance unavailable, short stack lines EconomyService.GetBalance() and GameDebugOptions.Coins, and Copy button. No web browser chrome. No screenshot or bug report button in this runtime app. Status footer Live / 42 entries / Collapse on.
HUD examples must look like performant tools rather than cards in a SaaS dashboard. All small dark cards with thin 2px Dreamy red top edge, tiny six-dot drag grip in top right with a REAL nonoverlapping 44-48-unit grip area. No large Dreamy logo in any HUD. FPS ONLY: inline 60 fps, small 16.7 ms, about 170x56 logical units. COMPACT: 60 fps | 16.7 ms with second aligned row RAM 414 MB, about 240x78. DETAILED: about 280x205, top row large 60 with fps unit and ms right, second row avg 59.8 / 1% 53 / .1% 47, thin mint frame history graph with amber threshold guide; lower two aligned columns Allocated 414 MB / Reserved 1068 MB and thin purple and amber memory traces. Audio is off in this concept. Do not draw new Render/Update/GPU timing values or huge green 277 FPS. Show only the three compact HUD examples with enough space between; a small separate footer label Off by default. Grip and numbers must never overlap.

Asset: board 03, Unity Editor Settings window and access/confirmation components. Compose LEFT 75 percent one large standalone flat Editor settings window, RIGHT 22 percent two small labeled components Access and Confirm. This is a Unity native tool window, not a web admin site. Native-style restrained header and project asset fields.
Editor header one Dreamy logo left, title Dreamy Debugger, small preview.6 tag. Below a compact project bar with Project configuration [SandboxDebuggerConfiguration] and small locate-object circle icon. Left sidebar exact five pages Overview / Access / Options / Performance / Diagnostics; Performance active with red indicator. Main section title Performance HUD and quiet description Off until enabled. At top right small Editor Preview indicator; no redundant setup/theme/acceptance buttons.
Main two-column body: left section Visibility has segmented selector Off(active in red-tinted selection) / FPS / Compact / Detailed; a labelled interactive-looking mini preview thumbnail with a 60 fps compact card and drag grip (explicit Preview label). Right section Placement has five compact choices Top left / Top right(selected) / Bottom left / Bottom right / Free, Scale 1.0x slider, Offset X 12 Y 12, switch Drag enabled On, button Reset position. Below: Display toggles Memory On and Audio Off; Thresholds rows Good 60 and Caution 30 each with small green/amber swatch; Low FPS warning toggle Off and collapsed Advanced. Use aligned labels and fixed-size value fields; no gigantic graphs or fake live metrics while Off. Footer a small line Configuration changes are saved to the selected asset, no author credits. Form sections have subtle separators rather than dozens of unrelated floating cards.
Right Access component: quiet dark modal title Unlock debugger, subtitle Enter PIN, four masked dots, readable numeric keypad with comfortable buttons and Back/Unlock controls. One small red top rule, no giant logo. Tiny caption outside PIN length is configurable. Right Confirm component: modal Add 100 coins?, description Uses the game wallet service., balance preview 9,825 to 9,925, secondary Cancel and red Confirm button. Do not display destructive reset as the default positive example. No extra buttons, no email/report form.
